frames.observation: The exact authored fish renderer is fully visible at native scale with a coherent head, seated eyes and mouth, continuous cream belly, paired flipper arms, long legs, and webbed feet. The foreground hero is a normal framing limit and does not cover the target.
The settled pre-attack stance preserves the same readable silhouette with shoulders, hips, limbs, face, and belly joined and no sampled floor or viewport clipping.

The causal native AttackCrit frame shows the fish rising from its stance with face, torso, flippers, legs, and feet still attached. Camera motion softens edge inspection and the bright ground effect covers the space below the feet.

The raised attack pose keeps both long arms and broad flipper hands connected to the shoulders while the belly, head, and legs remain coherent. Native success icons and ground light overlap small regions.

At the native AttackCrit contact and recovery boundary, the custom head, torso, arms, legs, and feet remain assembled. The hero and daze effect obscure the lower front of the fish and prevent fine hand-to-target inspection.

The final proficiency capture returns to a coherent idle fish with the exact renderer still visible and no sampled residual stretching, detached limb, or missing surface. Native wet bubbles and camera blur are presentation limits.
The ordinary no-focus action begins with the exact fish fully visible and coherent. Input UI covers the foreground hero but leaves the target surface readable.
The pre-impact target retains its full face, belly, arms, legs, and feet. This frame precedes the visible hit and does not establish damage deformation by itself.

The causal native Damaged frame is strongly occluded by the foreground hero and impact sphere. The exposed head and outside arm contours remain continuous, but the torso and inner limbs cannot be judged here.
The post-impact fish is readable behind the hero and damage number with its face, belly, flipper arms, legs, and feet still assembled. Foreground overlap limits the lower torso view.
The ordinary hit recovery restores the complete idle silhouette at HP 48 with no sampled shoulder separation, hip gap, eye displacement, tearing, or missing geometry.
The capture ends on a coherent idle fish after a later native enemy cycle, with the exact custom renderer visible and centered. This later cycle does not replace the earlier direct Damaged evidence.
The explicit fixture starts from an intact visible fish at HP 48. The action-selection UI is a normal foreground limit, and this baseline is not ordinary lethal evidence.
The causal native Death frame is strongly occluded by the hero and bright impact sphere. The exposed head and outside limb contours remain joined, while central deformation is not assessable here.

The custom fish is visibly launched backward in native Death with head, torso, flipper arms, legs, and feet still attached. Red native impact particles surround the body and are not credited as authored geometry.

The custom mesh is descending into its ragdoll collapse with the torso and long limbs still connected. The hero and damage number overlap the foreground; lingering pink impact particles limit fine floor inspection.
The defeated custom fish remains visibly collapsed with head, belly, paired arms, legs, and webbed feet forming a coherent corpse pose as combat UI clears.

The native gold-loot panel is open while the collapsed custom fish remains visible in the blurred background. This supports the sampled corpse handoff only; the overlay limits fine geometry inspection and the fixture does not establish ordinary lethal behavior or later corpse lifetime.
